title: The medieval world, 1000–1500 CE
reviewed: 2026-10-18. Each quote was copied from the linked article and is checked by npm run verify:sources.

events.title: The East–West Schism
events.summary: The Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches break communion. Scholars debate whether 1054 is the true turning point.

source.quote: preceded the formal split in 1054

events.title: The Norman Conquest of England
events.summary: William of Normandy defeats Harold Godwinson at Hastings and takes the English crown.

quote: 14 October at the Battle of Hastings

events.title: Teaching begins at Bologna
events.summary: Students in Bologna organize to hire teachers of law. It grows into Europe's oldest university.

source.quote: Teaching began around 1088

events.title: King John seals Magna Carta
events.summary: Rebel barons force the English king to accept limits on royal power.

source.quote: at Runnymede, near Windsor, on 15 June 1215

events.title: The Hundred Years' War
events.summary: England and France fight a long series of wars over the French throne.

source.quote: (French: Guerre de Cent Ans; 1337–1453)

events.title: The Black Death
events.summary: A plague pandemic sweeps across Europe and kills a large part of its people.

source.quote: occurred in Europe from 1346 to 1353

events.title: Gutenberg's printing press
events.summary: Johannes Gutenberg develops printing with movable metal type. His press later prints the Gutenberg Bible.

quote: in 1440 that he is said to have perfected
By 1450, the press was in operation

events.title: The fall of Constantinople
events.summary: The Ottoman army takes Constantinople after a 53-day siege. The Byzantine Empire ends.

source.quote: captured by the Ottoman Empire on 29 May 1453

events.title: Granada surrenders
events.summary: The last Muslim kingdom in Iberia surrenders to Castile. Jews are expelled from Spain the same year.

source.quote: On 2 January 1492, Muhammad XI of Granada (King Boabdil) surrendered

events.title: Crusaders take Jerusalem
events.summary: The First Crusade captures Jerusalem after a siege. The crusaders found the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

source.quote: from 7 June 1099 to 15 July 1099

events.title: Saladin retakes Jerusalem
events.summary: The Ayyubid sultan Saladin takes Jerusalem after the Battle of Hattin. The Third Crusade follows.

source.quote: from 20 September to 2 October 1187

events.title: The Mongols sack Baghdad
events.summary: Hulegu's Mongol army takes Baghdad and ends the Abbasid Caliphate there.

source.quote: took place in early 1258

events.image: File:Baybars, Medallion IV, Baptistère de Saint-Louis.jpg
events.title: The Mamluks stop the Mongols at Ain Jalut
events.summary: The Mamluks of Egypt defeat a Mongol army in Galilee. The Mongol advance west is halted.

source.quote: on 3 September 1260

events.title: Osman I founds the Ottoman state
events.summary: A Turkoman leader founds a small state in Anatolia. It grows into the Ottoman Empire.

source.quote: 1299 by the Turkoman tribal leader Osman I

events.title: The Tale of Genji is completed
events.summary: Murasaki Shikibu writes a long tale of the Japanese court. It is a classic of world literature.

source.quote: finished in its present form by 1021

events.title: Bi Sheng invents movable type
events.summary: A Song dynasty artisan prints with fired clay pieces, one for each character.

source.quote: invented between 1039 and 1048

events.title: The Kamakura shogunate
events.summary: Warrior families rule Japan through a military government at Kamakura.

source.quote: during the Kamakura period from 1185 to 1333

events.title: Genghis Khan unites the Mongols
events.summary: A council proclaims Temüjin ruler of all Mongols. His empire becomes the largest contiguous land empire.

source.quote: proclaimed as the ruler of all Mongols in 1206

events.title: Kublai Khan founds the Yuan dynasty
events.summary: The Mongol ruler Kublai Khan governs China as emperor of a new dynasty.

source.quote: lasted from 1271 to 1368 CE

events.image: File:A Seated Portrait of Ming Emperor Taizu.jpg
events.title: The Ming dynasty begins
events.summary: The Ming drive out the Mongol Yuan rulers. Ming emperors rule China for nearly three centuries.

source.quote: ruled from 1368 to 1644

events.title: Zheng He's treasure voyages
events.summary: A Ming admiral leads seven great fleets across the Indian Ocean. They reach Arabia and East Africa.

source.quote: Between 1405 and 1433, Zheng commanded seven treasure voyages

events.title: The Forbidden City is built
events.summary: The Ming build a vast palace complex in Beijing. It remains the imperial seat until 1924.

source.quote: constructed from 1406 to 1420

events.title: Timur builds an empire from Samarkand
events.summary: The conqueror Timur rules Central Asia and Iran from Samarkand.

source.quote: Timur established the empire in 1370 and ruled it until his death in 1405.

events.title: The great Chola temple at Thanjavur
events.summary: The Chola emperor Rajaraja I builds a towering temple to Shiva.

source.quote: between 1003 and 1010 CE

events.title: The Delhi Sultanate is founded
events.summary: Turkic rulers found a sultanate at Delhi. Its dynasties rule much of northern India for three centuries.

source.quote: The sultanate was established in 1206

events.title: The Vijayanagara Empire is founded
events.summary: Two brothers found a south Indian empire with its capital at Vijayanagara, now Hampi.

source.quote: It was established in 1336 by the brothers Harihara I and Bukka Raya I

events.title: Angkor Wat is built
events.summary: The Khmer king Suryavarman II builds a vast temple at his capital.

source.quote: constructed between 1113 and 1150 CE

events.title: The Majapahit Empire is founded
events.summary: Raden Wijaya founds a Javanese empire after a Mongol invasion. It comes to rule much of the archipelago.

source.quote: Established by Raden Wijaya in 1292

events.title: The Ayutthaya Kingdom is founded
events.summary: A Thai kingdom rises at Ayutthaya. It lasts for more than four centuries.

source.quote: existed in Southeast Asia from 1351 to 1767

events.title: Great Zimbabwe is built
events.summary: Shona builders raise great stone walls in southern Africa. The city becomes a royal capital.

source.quote: Major construction on the city began in the 11th century and continued until the 15th century.

events.title: The rock-hewn churches of Lalibela
events.summary: Churches are carved down into solid rock in the Ethiopian highlands. Tradition credits King Lalibela.

quote: following the capture of Jerusalem in 1187

events.title: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage to Mecca
events.summary: The ruler of Mali travels to Mecca with a vast entourage and much gold. Mali is at its height.

source.quote: Musa went on Hajj to Mecca in 1324

events.title: Kilwa builds the Husuni Kubwa palace
events.summary: A Swahili trading city on the East African coast builds a great palace.

source.quote: built the Husuni Kubwa palace in the 14th century

events.title: The Kingdom of Kongo is founded
events.summary: A marriage alliance joins two peoples into the Kingdom of Kongo in central Africa.

source.quote: The Kingdom of Kongo was founded around 1390

events.title: Songhai conquers Timbuktu and Djenné
events.summary: Sonni Ali of Songhai takes the great trading cities of the Niger.

source.quote: they were conquered in 1468 and 1475, respectively

events.title: Norse settlers reach Newfoundland
events.summary: Norse voyagers build a small settlement in North America. It is the only undisputed Norse site there.

source.quote: tree-ring dating of 1021

events.title: Cahokia at its height
events.summary: The Mississippian city by the Mississippi River has about 120 earthworks at its peak.

source.quote: At its apex around 1100 AD

events.title: The Inca rise in the Andes
events.summary: The Inca state grows from the highlands around Cusco. It later becomes the largest empire in the Americas.

source.quote: rose from the Peruvian highlands sometime in the early 13th century

events.title: The Mexica found Tenochtitlan
events.summary: The Mexica build their city on an island in Lake Texcoco. It becomes the Aztec capital.

source.quote: the date 13 March 1325 was chosen in 1925

events.title: Chan Chan, capital of the Chimú
events.summary: The Chimú rule the north coast of Peru from a vast adobe city. The Inca conquer them around 1470.

source.quote: from 900 to 1470, when they were defeated and incorporated into the Inca Empire

events.title: Columbus reaches the Caribbean
events.summary: Christopher Columbus lands in the Bahamas for Spain. Lasting contact between Europe and the Americas begins.

quote: They landed on the morning of 12 October.

events.title: Polynesians settle Hawaii
events.summary: Polynesian voyagers reach the Hawaiian Islands and settle them.

source.quote: puts the arrival of people at around 940–1130

events.title: Polynesians settle Rapa Nui
events.summary: Voyagers reach one of the most remote inhabited islands on Earth. Its people later carve the moai statues.

source.quote: the current best estimate for colonization is in the 12th century

events.title: Polynesians settle New Zealand
events.summary: East Polynesian voyagers settle New Zealand. Their descendants become the Māori.

source.quote: between 1320 and 1350 CE, when the main settlement period started
